title: viola odorata var. subcarnea
intro: Viola odorata var. subcarnea, commonly known as sweet violet, is a perennial plant species within the violet genus, characterized by its fragrant purple flowers and heart-shaped leaves. The sweet violet plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including reducing inflammation and promoting relaxation, which may be attributed to its therapeutic actions of being a natural anti-anxiety and anti-depressant agent. The bioactive constituents of sweet violet include flavonoids, such as rutin and kaempferol, as well as fragrances like vanillin, which contribute to its therapeutic properties. The plant's bioactive compounds are also thought to possess antimicrobial and antioxidant properties, further supporting its use in traditional medicine.
